rationale:
# QC threshold justification (from the supplied PBMC3k quantiles, histograms and scatter)

**Principle.** I chose inclusive cuts that remove only clear tails. The distributions are unimodal and continuous. There is no bimodal gap separating empty droplets or dead cells from real cells, so any cut inside the bulk would be arbitrary and would risk deleting real small or low-RNA cell types. The numbers below come from the observed quantiles and plots. I have not computed how many cells each cut removes. That count will be reported after filtering.

**Observed.** There are 2700 cells and 32738 genes, with 13 mitochondrial genes.
- Genes per cell: median 817, 1% quantile 326, 99% quantile 1749, max 3422. The histogram has a smooth left shoulder and a thin right tail. A few isolated cells lie at about 2400–3400 genes.
- Total counts: min 548, median 2197, 99% quantile 5929, max 15844. A few isolated cells lie above 10,000 counts.
- Mitochondrial fraction: median 2.0%, 95% quantile 4.0%, 99% quantile 5.9%. Almost all cells are below about 7%. A few isolated outliers lie at about 10% and about 22%.
- Genes vs counts: the scatter is tight and nearly log-linear. The few cells with elevated mitochondrial fraction sit at the low-count, low-gene end.

**Chosen thresholds.**
- **`min_genes = 300`.** This is just below the 1% quantile (326) and below the observed smooth lower shoulder. It removes only the extreme low-complexity tail, where the scatter shows the few high-mito cells concentrated. I did not use a higher cut such as 500 because that would cut about 5–10% of cells in the continuous left tail. That tail may contain real small or low-RNA cells, such as platelets, naive T cells and others. Even at 300, rare low-RNA populations may be partly lost. I will check that when I interpret small clusters.
- **`max_genes = 2500`.** The 99% quantile is 1749. The histogram shows a sparse tail beyond about 2000 and only a handful of isolated cells from about 2400 to 3400. A cut at 2500 removes only the most extreme of them and keeps the plausible high-complexity cells. Monocytes and other larger cells may legitimately have higher complexity.
- **`min_counts = 600`.** The minimum is 548 and the 1% quantile is about 659. Counts and genes are strongly correlated, so this is largely redundant with `min_genes`. It removes only the lowest few cells, which sit in the high-mito, low-complexity corner of the scatter.
- **`max_counts = 9000`.** The 99% quantile is about 5900. The histogram shows a continuous tail to about 7000 and then isolated cells above about 10,000. The cut at 9000 removes those isolated cells but keeps the continuous tail. The upper limit is roughly consistent with `max_genes`, since about 2500 genes corresponds to about 7500 counts on the observed trend.
- **`max_pct_mt = 8`.** The bulk of the distribution ends at about 6–7%, and the 99% quantile is 5.9%. Fresh PBMCs normally have low mitochondrial content, so cells at about 10% and about 22% look like outliers, possibly stressed or damaged cells. A cut at 8% removes them but does not cut into the bulk. I did not use the common 5% cut, because that would remove about 5% of cells in the tail of an otherwise continuous distribution. The cells between 5% and 8% are not clearly distinct from the main population.

## High-count and doublet caveats
- High counts and genes are only a weak proxy for doublets. The supported method family has no automatic doublet calling. The high-count tail cells lie along the same genes–counts trend as the other cells, so I cannot show that they are doublets. I treat the upper cuts as a conservative technical trim, not as doublet removal.
- Doublets with a typical total count, or heterotypic doublets with intermediate counts, will remain. I will watch for clusters that co-express lineage markers from two cell types, for example T-cell with myeloid markers or T-cell with B-cell markers. If such a cluster appears, I will report it as possibly doublet-like and not give it a confident biological label.
- Total counts and genes differ between cell types, so a single global upper cut can bias against large cells such as monocytes. I kept the upper cuts loose for that reason.

## Other limitations
- The data may already have been prefiltered upstream, since the minimum is 548 counts and 212 genes. The lower tail therefore does not show empty droplets.
- Because I did not apply a cut inside the bulk, residual library-size and mito effects remain, and regression is not available. I will check whether any cluster is driven by these covariates.
- These thresholds are a judgement made from one dataset. I will report how many cells each one removes, and I would not apply them to other datasets without re-inspection.
